notes: Markush generic. Formula II carries two variable substituents, R1 and R2, so the drawing does not determine a single compound and both name and smiles are null by rule 7. Ring numbering above is assigned by taking the carbon bearing HOOC as C1 and walking clockwise, which is the direction that reaches R1 next; every position is read off the drawn adjacencies, not inferred from what the compound ought to be. Stated as adjacencies alone, and independent of any numbering choice: HOOC and R1 are on adjacent vertices; R1 and CH2Br are on adjacent vertices; CH2Br and SO2R2 are on adjacent vertices; HOOC and SO2R2 are on opposite (para) vertices; the two remaining vertices are unsubstituted. Confidence is high because the page is born-digital and the ring, its three inner lines and all four substituent bonds are crisp at 8x zoom. The abstract text supplies the definitions R1 = fluorine, chlorine or bromine and R2 = (C1-C4)alkyl; those come from the prose, not from the drawing, and are not recorded as drawn substituent values. The drawing writes the R indices as SUPERSCRIPTS (R with a raised 1, R with a raised 2) while the abstract prose writes them as SUBSCRIPTS; see discrepancies. The label (II) to the right of the structure is the formula number, printed in the same right column at the level of the top of the drawing.

notes: MARKUSH GENERIC, formula II. The formula label '(II)' is printed in small type at the right-hand margin, level with the top of the drawing. name and smiles are null and must stay null: R1 and R2 are undefined variables in the drawing itself ([0010] and [0011] give R1 as fluorine, chlorine or bromine and R2 as (C1-C4)alkyl, so the drawing stands for a set of compounds, not one compound), and no single structure is determined. Ring drawn as a pointy-top hexagon: a vertex at top centre, a vertex at bottom centre, and vertical bonds forming the left and right sides. Positions below are read off that drawing, not inferred from any name. Going clockwise from the top vertex the six ring carbons are: top centre, upper right, lower right, bottom centre, lower left, upper left. The numbering used in the substituent list anchors C1 on the carbon bearing HOOC (the upper-left vertex, the only ring carbon with a carboxyl drawn on it) and counts clockwise through the substituted side, which is the direction that gives the substituents the lowest locants. So: upper left = C1 = HOOC, top centre = C2 = R1, upper right = C3, lower right = C4 = SO2R2, bottom centre = C5 and lower left = C6, both of which carry no drawn substituent (no H is written on them). Aromatic double bonds are drawn on three alternating edges as inner parallel lines. C3 bears a bromomethyl group drawn explicitly as two bonds: a bond from the ring carbon up and to the right to an unlabelled apex vertex (the CH2), then a bond down and to the right to the atom label 'Br'. C4 bears the label 'SO2R2' (S, subscript 2 O, R with superscript 2) on a single bond going down and right. C2 bears the label 'R1' (superscript 1) on a single bond going straight up. C1 bears the label 'HOOC' on a single bond going up and left, written right to left so the acidic H reads leftmost. presented_as is invention_route: [0004] immediately above introduces it as 'the present invention therefore provides a process for preparing 3-bromomethylbenzoic acids of the formula II', so this is the PRODUCT of the invention's process, not prior art.
